Implementation Plan

Implementation plan for #7095: close CI-triage issues whose failure is already fixed on main

Re-issued by the unblock judge from #6945.

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `f98e157049f142135fdc6d891371ed780a784cf6` on `main` (the planning context recorded `50badce…`; `main` has moved since). No integration branch is declared, so no mismatch is possible.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends the clarify.yml `Decide clarify route` gate (the `scripts/security_dependency.py` hold pattern) and `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` (`extract_failing_tests`, `filter_log`, `redact_secrets`, `neutralize_untrusted_routing`)
Scope-mode justification: The answers fix the scope. The check runs only in clarify.yml's "Decide clarify route" step (Q1: A), with no implement-time or poller checks. Evidence is the same check or shard succeeding on a default-branch commit that contains the linked PR's merge commit, and anything unreadable takes the normal path (Q2: A). A verified issue gets one evidence comment with a marker, then `ai:closed`, then a close as completed, and the merged PR is not touched (Q3: A). When resolution cannot be verified, the gate posts the failing shard's traceback using the heal intake's failing-test shapes (Q4: A); filing-time capture in `check_failure_triage.sh` is not added. A small new helper module is still needed. The gate needs PR, check-run, workflow-run, compare and job-log reads plus three writes, which do not belong in a 4,000-line heal module or in the security-dependency module. The module follows `security_dependency.py`'s CLI-and-JSON-verdict shape and imports the heal module's parsers instead of copying them (§6: correctness and safety come before speed).

Automation / §20 surface:
- One new helper script, `scripts/check_triage_resolution.py`. It is never run by hand: it is wired into the existing `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` route step, which runs on `issues: opened` and on trusted `/reclarify` comments (callers `internal-clarify.yml` and the consumer `ai-clarify.yml`).
- No new scheduler entry, no supervisor and no database work.
- It is not single-use, long-running or a supervisor, so it gets no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

---

1. Files likely to change

- `scripts/check_triage_resolution.py` (new): the gate logic (section 2).
- `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`:
  - Add `check_triage_resolution.py` to the "Stage workflow support files" list (line 238).
  - Call the gate in the "Decide clarify route" step (lines 423–518), after the security-dependency block.
  - Add `CHECK_TRIAGE_RESOLVED_GATE_ENABLED: ${{ vars.CHECK_TRIAGE_RESOLVED_GATE_ENABLED || 'true' }}` and `DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}` to the step's `env:`.
  - Add a `check_triage_resolved` output.
- `tests/test_check_triage_resolution.py` (new): unit and fixture tests plus a workflow wiring contract (section 6).
- `changelog.d/7095-check-triage-already-resolved.md` (new).
- `agents.d/7095-check-triage-already-resolved.md` (new). It documents:
  - the gate under workflow architecture item 13 (check failure triage);
  - the new stable log prefix `CHECK_TRIAGE_RESOLVED`.
- `README.md`: one variables-table row for `CHECK_TRIAGE_RESOLVED_GATE_ENABLED`.
- Explicitly not changed:
  - `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` (Q4: A).
  - `implement.yml`, `plan.yml`, the poller.
  - Every security-pass file (`review_single_issue_security_pass.sh`, `security_audit.sh`, the security-pass helpers in `orchestrate_poll_process.sh`). The spec forbids changing security-pass policy.

2. Functions / modules to implement (`scripts/check_triage_resolution.py`)

Style: tabs, `from __future__ import annotations`, argparse subcommand `gate`, one JSON object on stdout.

Shared parsing:
- Sibling-import `workflow_failure_heal` from `Path(__file__).parent`, the trusted staged `scripts/` directory.
- All GitHub reads go through one `_gh_api(args) -> Any` wrapper: `gh api` via `subprocess`, with a timeout and no retries of writes. Tests monkeypatch this wrapper.

Pure functions:
- `parse_triage_issue(issue) -> dict | None`
  - Returns `None` unless all of these hold:
    - the label `ai:check-triage` is present;
    - the author is trusted: a `User` with `author_association` OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR, or the `github-actions[bot]` Bot (same rule as `ISSUE_AUTHOR_TRUSTED`);
    - the body has exactly one line-leading `<!-- check-failure-triage:pr=<N> -->` marker outside fences, reusing the line-leading rule `check_failure_triage.sh` uses at lines 316–340.
  - Also extracts:
    - the check name from `- **Failing check:** \`<name>\``, which must be a single line without backticks;
    - an optional `- **Check run id:** \`<digits>\``;
    - the run id from `- **Check details:** https://github.com/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>…`.
  - Missing or duplicated fields return `{"malformed": reason}`, which leads to `unverified`.
- `find_resolved_marker(comments, pipeline_login, issue_number) -> dict | None`
  - Looks for a line-leading `<!-- ai:check-triage-resolved:v1 issue=<n> pr=<m> sha=<40hex> -->` on the last line of a comment authored by `pipeline_login`.
  - Comments from anyone else are ignored.
- `classify_check_runs(runs, expected_sha) -> "success" | <other>`
  - Returns `success` only when the list is non-empty, every run is `completed` with `conclusion == "success"` and has `head_sha == expected_sha`, and `total_count` does not exceed the list length (same strictness as the base gate at lines 410–412).
  - `neutral`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `failure`, `action_required`, `stale` and anything pending all return a non-success value. A failed check is never counted as passing.
- `shard_jobs_resolved(failed_job_names, base_jobs) -> bool`
  - True only when every failed PR job name, e.g. `orchestrate-poll (3)`, appears exactly once in the base run's job list with `conclusion == "success"`.
- `render_evidence_comment(...)` and `render_traceback_comment(...)` (section 4).

Network functions:
- `verify_resolution(repo, triage, default_branch) -> verdict`, in order:
  1. Read `repos/<repo>/pulls/<pr>`. Require `merged == true`, a 40-hex `merge_commit_sha`, and head repo == base repo. Otherwise `unverified reason=pr_not_merged|pr_unreadable`.
  2. Check-run triage (`Check run id` present):
     - Resolve the default-branch tip once with `repos/<repo>/commits/<default>` (the `.sha`).
     - Read `commits/<sha>/check-runs?check_name=<exact name>&filter=latest&per_page=100`.
     - Require `classify_check_runs == success`.
  3. Workflow-run triage (no check run id; the check name is the workflow name, e.g. `CI`):
     - Read `actions/runs/<run_id>`. Require `.name == check name`, `.repository.full_name == repo`, `.event == pull_request`, and that the run's `pull_requests[]` or `head_sha` matches the PR. Take its `workflow_id`.
     - Read `actions/runs/<run_id>/jobs?filter=latest&per_page=100` and collect the failed or timed-out job names.
     - Read `actions/workflows/<id>/runs?branch=<default>&event=push&status=completed&per_page=1` and take the newest completed push run. Require `conclusion == success` and its `head_sha`.
     - Read that run's jobs and require `shard_jobs_resolved`.
     - An empty failed-job list leads to `unverified reason=no_failed_jobs`, never to resolved.
  4. Read `repos/<repo>/compare/<merge_commit_sha>...<evidence_sha>`. Require `status` to be `ahead` or `identical`, so the evidence commit contains the PR's merge commit.
  5. Any exception, non-200, malformed JSON or missing field returns `unverified` with a fixed reason token. There is no partial success.
- `fetch_failing_tracebacks(repo, triage, failed_job_ids) -> list`
  - Job ids come from the check run id (an Actions check-run id equals its job id) or the failed jobs from step 3; at most 3.
  - Read `actions/jobs/<id>/logs`, pass the text through `filter_log` (which already applies `redact_secrets`), then `extract_failing_tests`.
  - Take a bounded excerpt: from the first `Traceback (most recent call last)` or `FAILED`/`FAIL:`/`ERROR:` line, at most 120 lines and 12 KB.
  - A 404 (a non-Actions check) or a read failure yields no excerpt; that path never fails the gate.
- `gate(args)`:
  1. Not a triage issue, or the gate is disabled: print `{"status":"not_triage"}` or `{"status":"disabled"}` and make no API call.
  2. Read the pipeline login from `gh api user --jq .login`.
  3. Read the issue comments once (paginated).
  4. If a trusted resolved marker exists, return `already_resolved` and only ensure `ai:closed` is applied and the issue is closed (both idempotent).
  5. Otherwise run `verify_resolution`.
     - On `resolved`: post the evidence comment, then add the `ai:closed` label (`GH_RETRY_IDEMPOTENT`-style single POST), then PATCH `state=closed state_reason=completed`. A write failure exits 3 with `reason=write_failed`.
     - On `unverified`: post at most one traceback comment per job id. Skip it if a trusted `<!-- ai:check-triage-traceback:v1 issue=<n> job=<id> -->` already exists. Exit 0.
  6. `--dry-run` prints the planned writes and makes none (used by the tests).

3. Data structures affected

- Verdict JSON on stdout: `{status: not_triage|disabled|already_resolved|resolved|unverified, reason, issue, pr, merge_sha, evidence_sha, evidence_url, check_name, failed_jobs: [...], traceback_posted: [job ids], writes: [...]}`.
- New comment markers, trusted only when authored by the `GH_PAT` login:
  - `<!-- ai:check-triage-resolved:v1 issue=<n> pr=<m> sha=<evidence_sha> -->` (Q3: A)
  - `<!-- ai:check-triage-traceback:v1 issue=<n> job=<id> -->`
- New clarify step output: `check_triage_resolved=true|false`.
- No state-file, label-contract or database changes. `ai:closed` and `ai:check-triage` already exist.
